name: Shephatiah
overview: Shephatiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah known specifically as the son of Mahalalel, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:4. His identification within the tribe highlights his place among the post-exilic community in Jerusalem. There are no additional notes that expand on his character or role beyond this genealogical detail.
namesAndTitles: The name Shephatiah means 'y-h-v-h has judged,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning tied to the judgment or justice of the Lord. This proper name, however, was not explicitly given by God but carries a clear theistic implication consistent with Hebrew naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shephatiah as the son of Mahalalel and suggests, by inference, that Amariah was his father. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shephatiah's mention in Nehemiah 11:4 situates him within the restored community of Judah after the Babylonian exile. His inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the continuity of God's people and the faithfulness of the tribe of Judah in maintaining their identity and heritage. Though brief, his presence affirms the ongoing fulfillment of God's promises to preserve His covenant people through successive generations.
